chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man found a dinar in his house. He said: 'Does someone else enter his house?' I said: 'Yes, frequently.' He said: 'This is a found object (luqata).' I said: 'But a man found a dinar in his chest (strongbox).' He said: 'Does someone else put his hand into his chest or place something in it?' I said: 'No.' He said: 'Then it is his.'

key_terms.دِينَار: A gold coin, used here as a unit of currency

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on money found in one's own house or chest according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between 'luqata' (found property) and personal wealth by establishing that possession within one's own dwelling or chest is presumed to be one's own unless external interference is proven. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'istishab al-bara'a' (presumption of innocence/original state), where the default status of items in one's private space is ownership rather than found goods. It provides a practical legal framework for resolving disputes over misplaced or forgotten assets within the home.
